The kit goes to 1.0.4, and the `fortress` and `notify` helpers built from it come along. The relay greets a browser with a short page and otherwise works as before.

## ✨ Added

- **Notifications say when a problem is over.** An event can be marked as a recovery, and a channel set to failures only carries it too, so whoever heard about the failure also hears that it ended. Apps set `Recovery` on `notify.Event`, and plugins hand `"recovery": true` to `notify send`.

## ⚡ Improved

- **The relay's address says what it is.** Opened in a browser, it shows a short page about the relay with a link to the project instead of a bare "404 page not found". Thanks to @Revan335 ([#18](https://github.com/junkerderprovinz/parleyport/issues/18)).
- **An opened page's websocket is dialed under a fixed host.** It could only ever reach the app's own pages, and now the host is fixed where the address is built.
- **golang.org/x/net 0.63.0** in the kit and in the helpers built from it. It carries the fix for a denial of service in the HTML parser ([GHSA-5cv4-jp36-h3mw](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-5cv4-jp36-h3mw)).

## 🐛 Fixed

- **A direct call stays on the path it was meant for.** Anyone holding the phrase could announce an address with a query or fragment in it, and a member's direct call then went as a POST to any page of a host the member could reach. Only the path of an announced address now comes before the call's own path.
- **A fortress frame is checked against its limit before any memory is set aside for it.** A head or body past the limit is refused instead of overflowing the size on a 32-bit system.
- **Members on a host with one network interface find each other on the local network.** On such a host, a container on a bridge network for example, the kit's local network service stopped right after it started. It neither heard the other members nor announced itself, so they could only meet through the relay. It keeps listening now.
- **A member that took a new phrase no longer shows up as gone.** When a member's answer got lost on the way back, the app that changed the phrase showed that member as left, although it already had the new phrase. The hand-over is tried again after a short pause, and a member that already has the new phrase simply confirms it.
- **The smart home dashboard shows an app again after a quick reconnect.** When the broker marked the dropped connection offline only after the app was already back, the device stayed unavailable until the next reconnect. The app now answers that late "offline" with "online".
- **The MQTT bridge reports its connection right after a reconnect.** When the loss was noticed only once the new connection stood, the bridge's status stayed at "lost" although it was connected.
